mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes during periods of clear rate hikes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.5 and UNRATE falls by >0.2pp m/m
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60d returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes with tight labor conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20d returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes with two-month RSAFS declines.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals a broad-based slowdown in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes with sharp INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in payroll employment (UNRATE up and PAYEMS down) signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 60d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals embedded inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to consider rate hikes and increases discount rates, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 yields positive 60d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes with sustained high CPI.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between housing starts (HOUST) and personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) falling together signals a broad-based weakening in household demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both fall in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20d returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where both HOUST and RSAFS decline simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held near zero for more than 12 months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.25% for >12 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 2.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves negative 60d returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during extended periods of near-zero rates and low inflation.
